rows.subtopic: Facing an ethical breach at work
rows.subtype: Approach: private conversation with the manager first [Action]
rows.description: The employee raises the concern calmly with a direct manager, describing what was observed and asking for clarification, and gives room for an honest explanation or correction.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, negotiation, seeking advice, values-first planning

rows.subtopic: Facing an ethical breach at work
rows.subtype: Approach: escalating to compliance if unresolved [Revision]
rows.description: When the manager dismisses the issue, the employee sends a written note to the compliance team or ethics helpline, following official process and avoiding gossip or social media.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: negotiation, seeking advice, values-first planning

rows.subtopic: Facing an ethical breach at work
rows.subtype: Approach: consulting a mentor outside the company [Action]
rows.description: The employee talks in general terms to a trusted mentor in another firm to test judgement and understand how others handled similar situations, without leaking confidential details.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, negotiation, values-first planning

rows.subtopic: Facing an ethical breach at work
rows.subtype: Approach: thinking through personal costs and protections [Thinking]
rows.description: The employee weighs risks to career and finances, checks the protections in company policy and law for those who report, and plans savings and a possible job search in case of retaliation.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, negotiation, seeking advice, values-first planning

rows.subtopic: Facing an ethical breach at work
rows.subtype: Approach: rationalising the wrongdoing as common practice [Pitfall]
rows.description: Colleagues say that everyone shaves numbers a little. The employee copies this reasoning, and small compromises grow until a serious problem cannot be hidden.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, seeking advice, values-first planning

rows.subtopic: Facing an ethical breach at work
rows.subtype: Approach: leaving when the culture will not change [Revision]
rows.description: After the company ignores repeated concerns, the employee decides that staying would mean joining the practice, and begins a planned search for a workplace whose values match.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, negotiation, seeking advice

rows.subtopic: Recovering from a major work mistake
rows.subtype: Approach: disclosing quickly and owning it [Action]
rows.description: After deleting a customer table by mistake, the engineer tells the lead within minutes, explains exactly what happened and what data is affected, so the team can start recovery at once.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, checklist, contingency planning, seeking advice

rows.subtopic: Recovering from a major work mistake
rows.subtype: Approach: hiding the mistake and hoping it goes unnoticed [Pitfall]
rows.description: The employee quietly patches the error and says nothing. When it appears later in an audit, the concealment damages trust far more than the original mistake would have.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: checklist, contingency planning, seeking advice

rows.subtopic: Recovering from a major work mistake
rows.description: The employee asks what can still get worse, stops the scheduled job, restores from backup and informs affected customers, and leaves blame and analysis for after the fire is out.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, checklist, seeking advice

rows.subtopic: Recovering from a major work mistake
rows.description: In the review, the team asks why the system allowed a single command to remove production data, and finds missing safeguards, weak permissions and no confirmation step.
